title: Butternut squash mac and cheese
equipment: 2-quart metal or ceramic baking dish (not glass, since it goes under the broiler)

items: 12 oz short pasta (such as cavatappi, shells or elbows)
2 Tbsp kosher salt (for the pasta water)
2 cups roasted or frozen butternut squash cubes
½ tsp kosher salt, plus more to taste
½ cup panko or crushed pepitas

steps: If using frozen squash, microwave it covered 5–6 min, stirring once, until soft all the way through. Set an oven rack 6 inches below the broiler.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil and add the 2 Tbsp salt. Cook the pasta 1 min less than the package says. Scoop out 1 cup pasta water, then drain.

Meanwhile, melt 1 Tbsp butter in the saucepan over medium heat. Add the garlic and cook 1 min, until fragrant. Scrape it into the blender with the squash and warm milk and blend until completely smooth.

Pour the purée back into the saucepan and warm over medium-low heat until steaming. Stir in the cheddar a handful at a time, then the parmesan, nutmeg and ½ tsp salt, until melted and smooth. Don't let it boil.
Add the pasta and stir to coat. Add pasta water a splash at a time until the sauce is creamy and loose. Taste and add salt and pepper.
Turn the broiler to high. Spread the pasta in the baking dish. Toss the panko with the melted butter and scatter it over the top.
Broil 2–3 min, until the top is golden. Watch it closely. Let it sit 5 min before serving.
tips: Shred your own cheddar. Pre-shredded cheese has anti-caking powder that makes the sauce grainy.
Skip the broiler if you're short on time. Toast the buttered panko in a skillet over medium heat 2–3 min and sprinkle it on.
Stir in browned Italian sausage for more protein.
storage: Fridge up to 4 days. Reheat in the microwave or a saucepan over low heat with a splash of milk. Freeze up to 2 months without the topping, then thaw overnight in the fridge before reheating.
